title: Consequences Of The Tech IPO Boom
gist: Chinese IPO issuance in 2026 is running at more than double last year's pace, capped by memory-chip maker CXMT raising at least RMB58bn on the Shanghai STAR market — the largest onshore fundraising since Alibaba's 2019 Hong Kong secondary listing. Gavekal's Thomas Gatley flags two historically recurring after-effects to size: liquidity being drained out of the equity market, ending the rally that began in 2024, and the cash triggering a fresh capex wave that deepens China's excess capacity.

themes.theme: Scale of the 2026 Chinese IPO wave

insights.claim: Memory-chip maker CXMT Corp. raised at least RMB58bn in its debut on the Shanghai STAR market, the largest fundraising on Chinese markets since Alibaba's RMB91bn Hong Kong secondary listing in 2019.
insights.speaker: Thomas Gatley
insights.so_what: A single deal of this size sets the benchmark for how much primary-market supply Chinese equities must absorb; track STAR-market issuance calendars and CXMT's post-listing performance as the sentiment gauge for the whole domestic tech complex.
insights.quote: CXMT raised at least RMB58bn—the biggest fundraising on Chinese markets since Alibaba’s RMB91bn secondary listing in Hong Kong in 2019
insights.locator: Initial public offerings by Chinese companies

insights.claim: Total Chinese IPO activity so far in 2026, both onshore and offshore, is running at more than double last year's pace.
insights.speaker: Thomas Gatley
insights.so_what: Doubling issuance is the cleanest quantitative marker that the supply/demand balance in Chinese equities is shifting; monitor monthly onshore plus Hong Kong IPO volumes as a leading indicator of liquidity stress.
insights.quote: total IPO activity so far this year, both onshore and offshore, is running more than double last year’s pace
insights.locator: Initial public offerings by Chinese companies

insights.claim: In Chinese market history, surges in equity fundraising have repeatedly withdrawn enough market liquidity to terminate an ongoing equity uptrend, putting the rally running since 2024 at risk.
insights.speaker: Thomas Gatley
insights.so_what: Treat heavy IPO supply as a tactical sell signal for Chinese equity beta, and watch whether regulators throttle the issuance pipeline to protect the index.
insights.quote: the withdrawal of market liquidity will mark the end of the upward trend in Chinese equities since 2024, as has happened so often in the past
insights.locator: For those familiar with Chinese market and macro history

insights.claim: The cash raised in the Chinese IPO boom is likely to fund a new wave of corporate capital expenditure, worsening China's excess-capacity problem.
insights.speaker: Thomas Gatley
insights.so_what: Points to renewed deflationary pressure and margin compression in newly funded sectors such as memory chips; short-list the industries where IPO proceeds are earmarked for capacity expansion.
insights.quote: this surge of cash will herald a new wave of capital expenditures and a worsening of excess capacity
insights.locator: Second, that this surge of cash

insights.claim: The analytical question posed is not whether the IPO boom has liquidity and capex after-effects but how large they will be, implying the historical playbook may overstate the damage this time.
insights.speaker: Thomas Gatley
insights.so_what: Frame the trade as a magnitude call: size IPO proceeds against total market turnover and against existing capex budgets before assuming the 2024-onward rally is over.
insights.quote: How big are these potential after-effects from Chinese technology firms cashing in on market enthusiasm?
insights.locator: How big are these potential after-effects
